stem: According to Jeremy, more words are better when writing.

flashcard.front: According to Jeremy (the instructor), should you have more words or less when writing?

keyFact: More words are better when writing: False, use fewer

stem: Why is it important to use correct grammar?
options: So you don't make a fool of yourself
It makes writing longer and more formal
It's only required in legal documents
It keeps emails short enough to read on a phone
why: Correct grammar enhances clarity and precision in writing and speech.

flashcard.front: Why is it important to use correct grammar?
flashcard.back: So you don't make a fool of yourself (it keeps writing clear and precise)

keyFact: Correct grammar: so you don't make a fool of yourself (clarity and precision)

stem: What do professional journalists and mass communicators use as a guideline for writing?
why: The deck lists AP Style for news releases and says to keep AP style for blogs and social media too.

flashcard.front: What do professional journalists and mass communicators use as a guideline for writing?

stem: What type of pyramid do journalists and mass communicators use as a writing guideline?
why: Inverted pyramid writing puts crucial information at the beginning, since readers could stop reading at any time.

flashcard.front: What type of pyramid, in particular, do journalists use as a guideline for writing?

stem: Per the Harvard Business Review figure in the deck, what share of businesspeople surveyed said poorly written materials waste workers' time?
keyFact: Businesspeople saying poor writing wastes time (HBR): 81%

stem: The deck cites Harvard Business Review as saying fuzzy writing allows fuzzy thinking.
why: The HBR points are that clarity builds trust, fuzzy writing allows fuzzy thinking, and a culture of clear writing makes managers more productive.

stem: What does the deck call the two biggest enemies of being concise?
why: The example drops both: "The banking department said there are numerous regulations coming down the pike to help consumers."
keyFact: Two biggest enemies of concise writing: "in order to" and "that"

stem: Gerunds are verbs, so they can replace verbs in a sentence.
why: Gerunds (words ending in -ing) are not verbs and cannot replace verbs. They are also an indicator of weak writing.

stem: Which of these sentences is written in active voice?
options: The cat was chased by the dog.
The cat was being chased by the dog.
The cat had been chased by the dog.
why: The deck rewrites "The cat was chased by the dog" as "The dog chased the cat."

stem: When writing to customers or elected officials, you should avoid writing more than how many words?
keyFact: Letters to customers/elected officials: avoid more than 400-600 words

stem: Which of these is NOT part of the deck's anatomy of a tweet?
why: A tweet is a question, a solution, a call to action, and a link to more info. A direct quote belongs to the news release list.

stem: Blogs are written for already-interested audiences.
why: Blogs should be kept relatively short, are written for already-interested audiences, and should keep AP style.

stem: When writing to customers or elected officials, save your opinion or reason for writing for the end.
why: State your opinion or reason for writing early, after a catchy introduction that sets the tone.

stem: Before writing, ask what your audience should know or think after reading. If the answer isn't immediately clear, what does the deck say?
options: You should call instead of writing
Your message needs a stronger subject line
why: Don't work out your thoughts while writing. If the answer isn't immediately clear, you're moving too quickly.

stem: The deck advises that comedy usually plays well in written communication.
why: Comedy usually doesn't play well, and there is no "sarcasm font." Use active voice and be concise.

stem: According to the deck, what gives a press release a better chance of being picked up?
options: Being closer to media style and writing format
Using the bank's own internal terms
Running longer than a full page
why: The closer the press release is to media style and writing format, the better chance it is picked up.
